name: Kisspeptin
used_for: A natural hypothalamic hormone that triggers release of GnRH and so luteinizing hormone (LH) and FSH. It is studied in academic clinical research on reproductive disorders (hypothalamic amenorrhea, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism), triggering egg maturation in IVF, and sexual desire, mostly in small trials. It is promoted online for libido, testosterone and fertility, though no approved product exists.

entries.text: Kisspeptin-54 as a single subcutaneous injection at 1.6 to 12.8 nmol/kg to trigger egg maturation after ovarian stimulation (uncontrolled dose-finding).

internet_entries.text: A peptide protocol site with affiliate links says people commonly use 100 mcg, 200 mcg or up to 500 mcg of kisspeptin two to three times per week, and also lists a weight-based range of 6 to 10 mcg per kg subcutaneously.
internet_entries.population: As described by the source, not a study population

administration_guidance.text: An educational peptide protocol site with affiliate supplier links says kisspeptin is often timed before sleep in community planning, that the mixed vial is kept refrigerated right away, and that its shelf life depends on the supplier's stated beyond-use limits rather than a fixed number of days. It also mentions rotating injection sites and letting the alcohol swab dry before injecting.
administration_guidance.label: internet

administration_guidance.text: In a randomized double-blind study in women with hypothalamic amenorrhea, kisspeptin-54 was given by subcutaneous injection twice daily for 2 weeks; the LH response to injection was much smaller by the last injection day than on the first, which the authors attributed to desensitization with repeated administration.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: A kisspeptin dosing site that earns affiliate commissions from vendor links says injections are placed about an hour before bed, in the lower abdomen or upper outer thigh with site rotation, that a mixed vial is refrigerated and used within about 28 days, and that use is cycled with off periods to avoid receptor desensitization. It says nothing about missed doses and gives no fasting requirement.
administration_guidance.label: internet

side_effects.text: In a randomized crossover trial of a single intravenous kisspeptin-54 infusion in women with hypoactive sexual desire disorder, kisspeptin was reported as well tolerated.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: In a trial of women at high risk of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) given kisspeptin-54 as an egg-maturation trigger, no woman developed moderate to critical OHSS.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: A study of twice-weekly kisspeptin-54 injections for up to 8 weeks in women with hypothalamic amenorrhea reported no adverse effects, in a very small sample.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: The same protocol site says reported effects include mild flushing or warmth shortly after injection, mild injection-site redness, transient headache and brief nausea.
side_effects.label: internet

internet_claims.claim: A functional medicine clinic page promotes kisspeptin therapy as a breakthrough that restores libido, fertility and sex hormones naturally without suppressing the body, and invites readers to book a consultation. It presents the benefits without citing human trials, and the page sells the service.

A telehealth company article says kisspeptin is not a testosterone drug or shortcut to hormone optimisation, that studies show LH rises and sometimes modest testosterone rises, and that most kisspeptin therapy remains in research settings. The company sells peptide protocols.

A retail-pharmacy peptide information page says kisspeptin is not an approved fertility, testosterone or libido treatment, that research-only products are not approved for human use, and that vendor vials differ from FDA-approved medicines in purity and dosing.

research.summary: Dose-finding study (J Clin Invest) of a single kisspeptin-54 injection to trigger egg maturation in 53 women having IVF, without a comparison group (registered as NCT01667406).
research.finding: Eggs matured at every dose, 92% of women had embryo transfer, and clinical pregnancy was 23%. There was no control group, so it cannot show kisspeptin works better than standard triggers.

research.summary: Phase 2 open-label randomized dose study (J Clin Endocrinol Metab) of kisspeptin-54 as an egg-maturation trigger in 60 women at high risk of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS).
research.finding: Eggs matured in 95% of women, no woman developed moderate to critical OHSS, and live birth rate per transfer was 45%. It had no standard-trigger comparison arm.

research.summary: Phase 2 randomized, blinded trial (Hum Reprod) of one versus two kisspeptin-54 doses in 62 women at high risk of OHSS.
research.finding: A second dose improved the share of women reaching a high oocyte yield (absolute difference 26 points, P = 0.042), with no increase in moderate OHSS. Authors note the need to compare with established triggers.

research.summary: Randomized, double-blind study (J Clin Endocrinol Metab) of twice-daily kisspeptin-54 injections for 2 weeks in 10 women with hypothalamic amenorrhea.
research.finding: The first dose strongly raised LH and FSH, but the response had mostly vanished by day 14 (tachyphylaxis, loss of effect), and ovarian activity did not change. A key limit for repeated use.

research.summary: Study (Clin Pharmacol Ther) of twice-daily versus twice-weekly kisspeptin-54 for up to 8 weeks in women with hypothalamic amenorrhea.
research.finding: Twice-weekly dosing caused only partial desensitization and hormone levels were higher than with saline at 8 weeks, with no adverse effects reported. Very small study with hormone endpoints, not fertility outcomes.

research.summary: Randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled crossover trial (JAMA Netw Open) of an intravenous kisspeptin-54 infusion in women with hypoactive sexual desire disorder, with brain imaging.
research.finding: Kisspeptin changed brain responses to erotic and attractive-face stimuli and was well tolerated, but the outcome was brain activity in 32 completers after a single infusion, not sexual function in daily life.

research.summary: Recruiting phase 2 trial (Massachusetts General Hospital, FDA-regulated drug study) of two weeks of pulsatile subcutaneous kisspeptin in men and women with idiopathic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, planned 36 participants (record updated 2026-07-13).
research.finding: No results are posted yet. The record describes an investigational physiology study of hormone release and ovarian follicle growth.

research.summary: Dose-response and infusion study of kisspeptin-10 in healthy men, with 4 to 6 men per part (George et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab).
research.finding: Intravenous boluses raised luteinizing hormone (LH) in a dose-dependent way, peaking at 1 microgram per kg, while 3 micrograms per kg gave a smaller response. A 1.5 microgram per kg per hour infusion raised LH pulse frequency, and a 22.5-hour infusion raised testosterone.

research.summary: Randomized, single-blinded, placebo-controlled study (Yeung et al., Eur J Endocrinol) of subcutaneous kisspeptin-10 infusions in 15 healthy men, including 5 days of continuous infusion and 12 days of daily 8-hour infusions.
research.finding: Continuous infusion for 5 days kept testosterone up but gonadotropins fell back to vehicle levels. Daily 8-hour infusions kept LH and FSH raised for 12 days (mean LH rise +1.68 on day 1 and +1.14 on day 12), and the receptor still responded to a bolus afterward. The study used infusions, not injections.

research.summary: Double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study in 6 healthy men of a 90-minute intravenous kisspeptin-54 infusion (Dhillo et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab).
research.finding: Kisspeptin-54 raised LH (10.8 vs 4.2 U/liter), follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and testosterone versus saline. Its blood half-life was about 27.6 minutes.

research.summary: Genetic study of a family and one unrelated patient with absent puberty, plus a mouse model with the same receptor gene removed (Seminara et al., N Engl J Med).
research.finding: People and mice lacking a working GPR54 (the kisspeptin receptor) did not go through puberty but still responded to gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH), which places kisspeptin signaling above GnRH.

research.summary: Small study (4 to 5 per group) of kisspeptin-10 given intravenously or subcutaneously to healthy men and women (Jayasena et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab).
research.finding: Men responded with higher LH and FSH. Women in the follicular phase of the cycle showed no response even at the highest doses, while women in the preovulatory phase did respond.

research.summary: FDA web page on bulk drug substances for compounding that may present significant safety risks (content current as of 22 April 2026, fetched 2026-09-30).
research.finding: Kisspeptin-10 is listed in category 2 for section 503A compounding (added 29 September 2023). FDA says compounded kisspeptin-10 may pose immunogenicity and impurity risks and that it has no or limited safety information for the proposed routes. This does not make kisspeptin an approved drug.

dose.summary: No approved dose exists. Trials gave kisspeptin-54 by weight, for example 1.6 to 12.8 nmol/kg under the skin before egg collection in in vitro fertilization (IVF), and kisspeptin-10 mostly by vein or infusion. Online sources describe 50 to 500 mcg of kisspeptin-10, which differs from the by-weight doses studied.

items.text: Peptide Dosing Protocols, a site that earns supplier commissions, lists 50 to 100 mcg of kisspeptin-10 as a low dose and 100 to 200 mcg as a standard dose. It says these are community ranges based partly on kisspeptin-54 trial data.

timing.summary: No study tested time of day. In IVF trials eggs were collected 36 hours after the injection, and in women kisspeptin-10 worked only in the preovulatory part of the cycle. Online sources say bedtime or morning, which is untested.

items.text: In IVF trials, eggs were collected 36 hours after the kisspeptin-54 injection. This timing was set by the egg-collection schedule, not tested against other times.
items.label: research

items.text: In healthy women, kisspeptin-10 raised LH and FSH during the preovulatory phase but not in the follicular phase, even at high doses. Men responded at low doses.
items.label: research

items.text: A peptide protocol site with affiliate links says kisspeptin is often timed before sleep in community planning.
items.label: internet

items.text: A kisspeptin dosing site that earns affiliate commissions says injections are placed about an hour before bed.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Initiative says morning dosing works well for most goals and ties it to the body's natural cortisol rise on waking. It says fertility timing may be adjusted by cycle phase.
items.label: internet

fasting.summary: No study tested food or fasting with kisspeptin. One educational site says food timing does not matter.

items.text: Peptide Initiative says kisspeptin can be taken regardless of food timing and that meals do not much change absorption of an injection.
items.label: internet

frequency.summary: Trials used single doses for IVF. Twice-daily injections lost most of their effect within 2 weeks, while twice-weekly injections kept a partial effect. Online sources describe daily dosing or two to three times a week, and skipping a missed dose.

items.text: In women with hypothalamic amenorrhea, kisspeptin-54 twice daily raised LH by 24.0 IU/liter on the first injection day but only by 2.5 by day 14. The authors called this desensitization.
items.label: research

items.text: Twice-daily kisspeptin-54 nearly abolished the FSH response by day 2 and gradually reduced the LH response. Twice-weekly injections caused only partial desensitization.
items.label: research

items.text: In women having IVF at high risk of OHSS, a second kisspeptin-54 dose 10 hours after the first raised the share reaching a high egg yield from 45% to 71%. It did not raise moderate OHSS.
items.label: research

items.text: In 7 healthy men, kisspeptin-10 infused for 8 hours then paused for 16 hours each day kept LH raised. Continuous infusion for 5 days did not.
items.label: research

items.text: A registered, ongoing phase 2 trial (NCT05896293) gives subcutaneous kisspeptin in pulses every 60 to 240 minutes for two weeks in people with idiopathic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. No results are posted and the exact dose is not stated.
items.label: research

items.text: A peptide protocol site that earns affiliate commissions says people commonly use kisspeptin two to three times per week.
items.label: internet

items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Dosing Protocols, a site that earns supplier commissions, lists once-daily injections of 50 to 200 mcg, or 100 mcg twice daily as a split dose. It says a missed dose is usually skipped rather than doubled.
items.label: internet

cycle_length.summary: Trials ran from a single dose to 8 weeks, and the longest used twice-weekly injections. No study tested stopping or restarting. Online sources describe cycles of 2 to 6 weeks with breaks, which no trial has tested.

items.text: After 2 weeks of twice-daily kisspeptin-54, women remained responsive to GnRH. The loss of response was to kisspeptin, not to the pituitary.
items.label: research

items.text: Twice-weekly kisspeptin-54 for 8 weeks left hormone levels higher than saline at 8 weeks, with no adverse effects reported. This very small study measured hormones, not fertility.
items.label: research

items.text: Daily 8-hour subcutaneous kisspeptin-10 infusions for 12 days kept LH and FSH raised (LH rise +1.68 on day 1 and +1.14 on day 12) in healthy men.
items.label: research

items.text: A kisspeptin dosing site that earns affiliate commissions says use is cycled with off periods to avoid receptor desensitization.

items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Initiative says powder is kept in the fridge short term or the freezer long term, and a mixed vial is refrigerated, never frozen, and used within 14 to 21 days. It lists belly, thigh and upper arm as injection sites and says to discard cloudy or discolored vials.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Dosing Protocols, a site that earns supplier commissions, says powder is kept at -20 C and a mixed vial at 2 to 8 C, not frozen. It says to discard a cloudy vial and to respect the supplier's beyond-use limit.
items.label: internet

mechanism.summary: Kisspeptin is a natural brain hormone that acts above gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH), which tells the pituitary to release luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH). In men LH then raises testosterone. Kisspeptin-54 lasts about 28 minutes in blood.

items.text: People and mice lacking a working kisspeptin receptor (GPR54) did not go through puberty but still responded to GnRH. This places kisspeptin signaling above GnRH.
items.label: research

items.text: In 6 healthy men, a 90-minute kisspeptin-54 infusion raised LH, FSH and testosterone versus saline. Its blood half-life was about 27.6 minutes.
items.label: research

items.text: In healthy men, a kisspeptin-10 infusion raised LH pulse frequency and size, which fits an action on the GnRH pulse generator.
items.label: research

best_documented_effect.summary: Best result is as an IVF egg-maturation trigger. Eggs matured in 95% of 60 women at high risk of OHSS with no moderate or worse OHSS, but there was no comparison with standard triggers. Other uses are tested only for hormone or brain effects.

items.text: In 60 women at high risk of OHSS, a single kisspeptin-54 injection matured eggs in 95%, no woman developed moderate to critical OHSS, and live birth was 45% per transfer. There was no standard-trigger arm.
items.label: research

items.text: In the first 53-women study, eggs matured at every dose, 92% had embryo transfer and clinical pregnancy was 23%. There was no control group.
items.label: research

items.text: In 10 women with hypothalamic amenorrhea, 2 weeks of twice-daily kisspeptin-54 did not change LH pulsatility or ovarian ultrasound findings.
items.label: research

items.text: In women with low sexual desire, one kisspeptin-54 infusion changed brain responses to erotic and attractive-face images. The outcome was brain activity in 32 women, not sexual function in daily life.
items.label: research

side_effect_groups.title: In trials
side_effect_groups.summary: Small trials reported kisspeptin as well tolerated. No woman at high risk of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) had moderate or worse OHSS.

items.text: In a randomized crossover trial of a single intravenous kisspeptin-54 infusion in women with hypoactive sexual desire disorder, kisspeptin was reported as well tolerated.
items.label: research

items.text: In a trial of women at high risk of OHSS given kisspeptin-54 as an egg-maturation trigger, no woman developed moderate to critical OHSS.
items.label: research

items.text: A study of twice-weekly kisspeptin-54 injections for up to 8 weeks in women with hypothalamic amenorrhea reported no adverse effects, in a very small sample.
items.label: research

side_effect_groups.title: Online reports
side_effect_groups.summary: Online sources list mild flushing, injection site redness, headache and nausea. These come from sellers or education sites, not from trials.

items.text: A protocol site with affiliate links says reported effects include mild flushing or warmth shortly after injection, mild injection-site redness, transient headache and brief nausea.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Initiative says flushing, injection site reactions and mild headache are common, and a faster heart rate or dizziness is less common. It says to stop for allergic reactions, persistent flushing, or large rises in blood pressure or heart rate.
items.label: internet

side_effect_groups.title: Regulator warning
side_effect_groups.summary: The FDA lists kisspeptin-10 among compounding substances that may carry significant safety risks. No kisspeptin product is approved.

items.text: The FDA lists kisspeptin-10 in category 2 for section 503A compounding, added 29 September 2023. It says compounded drugs may pose immunogenicity risk and impurity concerns and that it has no or limited safety information for the proposed routes.
items.label: research
